summary: calorimeter_resolution.py fitted sigma_E/E without per-point errors with unit weights on (sigma/E)^2, which biased the constant term and often gave a negative squared term.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the defective code is in the script as first released (hep-research 0.3.0, commit 351029c0)
database_specific.outputs: skills/hep-detector/scripts/calorimeter_resolution.py prints JSON on stdout (points, weighting, ndof, energy_range_gev, stochastic_squared and the other resolution terms) and writes no artifact

observables: stochastic, noise and constant terms of the calorimeter resolution fit (calorimeter_resolution.py --fit)
impact.bias: in 2000 toys with 2% scatter and a true constant term c = 0.0070, unit weights gave c^2 < 0 in 26% of the fits and a mean c of 0.0083 in the rest (now 0.0070, sd 0.00013)
impact.trigger: a fit given points without per-point uncertainties (energy and resolution pairs only)

remedy: refit with a release that has the fix (or give per-point uncertainties); a constant term from the old fit is biased high
